extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in podcasts / Joe Rogan
extracted.subtask_short: podcast profile: the joe rogan experience
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article summarizing the history, format, guests, controversies, production, distribution, and influence of the Joe Rogan Experience podcast. The page describes how the show is produced, labeled, distributed, and received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode length
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Episodes are typically long-form; some episodes have lasted over five hours (e.g., episode no. 1,530 lasted over five hours). Use of very long runtimes is a characteristic feature of the show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode types / format labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: There are at least four types of episodes, as labeled on YouTube and Spotify: the 'main' general category, 'JRE MMA Show', 'Protect our Parks', and the 'Fight Companion' episodes (which are streamed live).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Episodes are explicitly labeled on distribution platforms; format labels distinguish live streams, themed shows, and the main interview format. Highlight clips vs full episodes are used on different platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guest diversity and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The podcast includes a wide array of guests — entertainers, academics, comics, UFC fighters, and other non-political figures — plus ideologically diverse political guests and public figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-profile and varied guests (e.g., Elon Musk, Kanye West, Edward Snowden, Bernie Sanders, Neil deGrasse Tyson, Donald Trump) are central to the show's identity and reach; guest mix affects audience, controversy potential, and influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent publishing schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintaining a consistent schedule was important in jumpstarting the podcast's growth; it soon grew to two episodes a week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistency in release cadence is cited as a factor in audience growth and discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production roles and technical skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Production historically involved a sole co-host/producer (Brian Redban) and later additional producers (Jamie Vernon); producers film, produce, and edit episodes and operate audio equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producers' technical competence (audio/video engineering, editing) and staffing levels affected the ability to increase frequency and episode length; self-taught skills and role transitions are noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording location / studio setup
rubrics_metrics.description: The podcast was originally recorded at Rogan's home, then moved to a private studio in Woodland Hills, Los Angeles, and later production relocated to Austin, Texas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recording environment and studio infrastructure relate to production quality, logistics, and changes in format or output after platform deals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health and safety procedures for guests (COVID-era)
rubrics_metrics.description: In April 2020, Rogan began having guests take an antibody test for COVID-19 before recording the podcast, using a personalized service offering each test for $299.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-recording health precautions were adopted during the pandemic to enable continued production; such measures are part of operational standards in case of public-health risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform distribution and exclusivity/licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: The podcast became exclusively available on Spotify (December 2020–February 2024) under a licensing deal; highlight clips continued on YouTube; later returned to YouTube and other platforms after a new contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform licensing choices affect where full episodes and highlights are available, visibility, monetization, and public response. Exclusivity can lead to removal or absence of past content on other platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform content policies and moderation
rubrics_metrics.description: Platform actions cited include Spotify defending episodes as within content guidelines, YouTube taking down episodes for violating COVID-19 misinformation rules, and Spotify adding content advisories for COVID-related episodes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance (or noncompliance) with platform policies can cause episode removals, advisories, or internal company disputes; platforms may apply misinformation or offensive-content policies which affect availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to controversial content and host conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Rogan has been criticized for hosting far-right guests, accused of using racially insensitive language, and criticized for comments about COVID-19 vaccines; these controversies prompted public backlash, artist withdrawals, and episode removals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host speech and guest viewpoints are evaluative dimensions influencing reputation, platform decisions, and corporate/artist responses (e.g., musicians removing catalogues from Spotify). Public apologies and explanations are part of damage control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsorship and monetization decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The podcast's first sponsor was Fleshlight (May 2010); later large licensing deals with Spotify were made (estimated $200 million in 2020 and $250 million in 2024).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsorships and platform deals shape financial sustainability, distribution choices, and public perception (e.g., comparisons of creator payouts vs artist royalties). Sponsors may also withdraw if issues arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of highlights vs full-episode publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: When the show moved to Spotify, full episodes were removed from YouTube after December 2020 while highlight clips continued to be uploaded; upon return to non-exclusive distribution, full episodes reappeared on other platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions about publishing full episodes vs clips affect discoverability, viral potential, and platform moderation; platform search visibility and algorithmic prominence also matter (YouTube search visibility issues noted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience reach and influence metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics referenced include monthly downloads/listens (e.g., 11 million listeners in Jan 2015; 16 million downloads/month by Oct 2015; 190 million downloads/month in 2019) and viral view counts (e.g., 26 million views in first 24 hours for a 2024 episode).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High reach is used as evidence of cultural and political influence (impacts on book sales, candidate fundraising, and public debate). Engagement metrics serve as proxies for influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and industry recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: The podcast won a Stitcher Award for Best Overall Show of 2013 and Best Comedy Podcast at the iHeartRadio Podcast Awards in 2019.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry awards and rankings (e.g., iTunes top 100) are presented as signals of quality or prominence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live streaming and audience interaction methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Early production used live streams on Justin.tv and Ustream with chatroom interaction; the format emphasized live interaction with fans and an open-discussion style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Live streaming and direct audience interaction were part of the early growth strategy and influence the show’s informal tone and format choices.
